summary:
ASTRA is an interactive Mars traverse planning and mission-simulattion platform that helps users turn NASA planetary data into safer more informed mobility decisions. By selecting start and destination points on a 3D  Mars globe, users can generate and compare compliant routes against hazardous alternatives, with terrain-driven risk insights derived from NASA MOLA elevation data-including slope and grade analysis, hazard awareness, and clear visual safety cues

ASTRA integrates NASA Mars Trek imagery for geospatial context and realtime NASA/JPL Curiosity REMS weather data to ground planning in authentic mission conditions. Beyond route planning, it supports traverse preview/simulation and mission-oriented workflows that make complex environmental constraints easier to understand and communicate.

To keep terrain-intensive operations responsive, ASTRA accelerates key DEM computations(elevation sampling, heightmaps, slope analysis, and pathfinding) with in-process Rust kernels alongside Python services. By transforming raw datasets into explainable, actionable guidance. ASTRA advances safer Mars exploration planning and makes planetary science more accessible.
details:
What it does & how it works:
ASTRA is an online tool to simulate and plan traversing on Mars. Users pick a starting and ending location on a 3D interactive globe of Mars and have ASTRA provide both a safe/compliant path and compare it to a dangerous/straight path. By using NASA MOLA DEM data, ASTRA can sample the data to find slopes, grades, hazards, and create paths (using A* based on terrain constraints). Users can see this data on top of NASA Mars Trek layers/imaging along with real-time weather from NASA/JPL Curiosity REMS (source-cited), presented in context about the mission/scientific goals. Users can both preview/simulate traversal, see warnings about hazards, and utilize a reset/first launch walkthrough to easily use the tool.


Benefits

  • Clear indication of safety/slopes to provide explainable best paths
  • Can be easily interpreted due to being based on one streamlined process using imagery, terrain, and weather data
  • Provides mission context to discuss, learn about, and plan
  • Can quickly be interpreted due to efficiently calculating terrain data.

Intended impact
Overall, ASTRA is intended to both limit the danger of moving on Mars by identifying hazards as early as possible and to easily make NASA data more readable and available to students, scientists, and in discussions about the mission.


Tools, languages, hardware & software

  • Frontend: CesiumJS, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Zustand
  • Backend: Python using FastAPI
  • Efficiency: Using Rust for DEM kernels (A*, heightmaps, slopes, terrain) through PyO3 as an in-process tool, or using Python if Rust is not available
  • Data used: NASA/PDS MOLA, NASA/JPL Curiosity REMS, NASA Mars Trek, USGS for context
  • Development: Using Node.js/npm, Git/GitHub, Cargo; No specialized hardware other than standard computers and browsers.


Creativity & factors considered:
Overall, creativity was using various NASA data sources to combine into one streamlined, explainable process from planning to simulation. We wanted our data to be accurate and credited, to clearly illustrate safety, to be efficient and maintainable, and to be easy to use in order to turn complicated terrain constraints into something manageable.
